CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bengkayang Regency. 2. Regional Government is Bengkayang Regency as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkayang Regency. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Institution of Bengkayang Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 6. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government and regional government. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 8. Child with Special Needs is a child with special characteristics that differ from children in general without always indicating mental, emotional or physical disability, which includes among others: visually impaired, hearing impaired, mentally disabled, physically disabled, socially maladjusted, learning difficulties, behavioral disorders, gifted children, children with health disorders and disabled children. 9. Child Protection is all forms of activities to guarantee and protect children so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with dignity and humanity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect. 11. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 15. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at: preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 17. Violence is any act that results in or causes suffering and distress whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 18. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 19. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 20. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 21. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss due to the actions of others. 23. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 25.

I. GENERAL

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high averaging per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases / acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious attention and handling.

In connection with this, the Government of Bengkayang Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Organization of Protection for Women And Child Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

Article 19

1. In organizing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government shall include consultation, coordination, and reporting.
3. Cooperation with other regional governments and other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, and development of integrated service systems.

Article 18

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 11 letter f, shall include monitoring, documentation, and reporting of cases of violence against women and children.

CHAPTER III

SCOPE

Article 4

The scope of protection of women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, obligations and authority of the Regional Government, implementation of protection, reporting, control, guidance and supervision, community participation and financing.

Article 12

1. Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 11 letter a include:
a. forming a network for prevention and handling of violence through coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
b. forming a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence;
c. organizing communication, information, and education about violence against women and children; and
d. socialization of laws and regulations related to violence against women and children.
2. Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner coordinated by the SKPD having duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment.

CHAPTER VIII

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 22

1. The Regent shall carry out control, guidance, and supervision of the organization of protection for victims of violence against women and children.
2. Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

CHAPTER VII

REPORTING

Article 21

1. P2TP2A shall report prevention, handling and protection activities for women and child victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment.
2. The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment shall report prevention, handling and protection activities for women and child victims of violence to the Regent.
3. The Regent shall report protection of women and child victims of violence to the Governor.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 15

Legal protection as referred to in Article 11 letter c includes:
a. providing protection in shelters;
b. providing assistance in legal processes; and
c. providing special legal protection for child victims of violence which may be carried out by appointing guardianship in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 8

In implementing protection for women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by P2TP2A.

Paragraph 3

Legal Protection

Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A for the Protection of Women and Children is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 26. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 27. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved. 28. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children. 29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims. 33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 24

Financing of activities related to the organization of protection for women and child victims of violence may be sourced from:
a. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Provincial Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
c. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or
d. other lawful and non-binding sources.

Article 2 letter a

What is meant by "respect for victims' rights" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights.

letter b

What is meant by "justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying development results.

letter c
What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.

letter d
What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration.

letter e

What is meant by "non-discrimination" means not making distinctions on any grounds or in any manner, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bengkayang Regency. 2. Regional Government is Bengkayang Regency as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkayang Regency. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Institution of Bengkayang Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 6. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government and regional government. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 8. Child with Special Needs is a child with special characteristics that differ from children in general without always indicating mental, emotional or physical disability, which includes among others: visually impaired, hearing impaired, mentally disabled, physically disabled, socially maladjusted, learning difficulties, behavioral disorders, gifted children, children with health disorders and disabled children. 9. Child Protection is all forms of activities to guarantee and protect children so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with dignity and humanity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect. 11. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 15. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at: preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 17. Violence is any act that results in or causes suffering and distress whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 18. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 19. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 20. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 21. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss due to the actions of others. 23. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 25.

CHAPTER III

SCOPE

Article 4

The scope of protection of women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, obligations and authority of the Regional Government, implementation of protection, reporting, control, guidance and supervision, community participation and financing.

Article 18

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 11 letter f, shall include monitoring, documentation, and reporting of cases of violence against women and children.

Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A for the Protection of Women and Children is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 26. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 27. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved. 28. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children. 29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims. 33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

Article 19

1. In organizing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government shall include consultation, coordination, and reporting.
3. Cooperation with other regional governments and other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, and development of integrated service systems.

I. GENERAL

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high averaging per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases / acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious attention and handling.

In connection with this, the Government of Bengkayang Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Organization of Protection for Women And Child Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

Article 12

1. Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 11 letter a include:
a. forming a network for prevention and handling of violence through coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
b. forming a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence;
c. organizing communication, information, and education about violence against women and children; and
d. socialization of laws and regulations related to violence against women and children.
2. Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner coordinated by the SKPD having duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment.

CHAPTER VIII

Article 22

1. The Regent shall carry out control, guidance, and supervision of the organization of protection for victims of violence against women and children.
2. Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 15

Legal protection as referred to in Article 11 letter c includes:
a. providing protection in shelters;
b. providing assistance in legal processes; and
c. providing special legal protection for child victims of violence which may be carried out by appointing guardianship in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

SCOPE

Article 12

a. forming a network for prevention and handling of violence through coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;

c. organizing communication, information, and education about violence against women and children; and
d. socialization of laws and regulations related to violence against women and children.

I. GENERAL

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high averaging per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases / acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious attention and handling.

In connection with this, the Government of Bengkayang Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Organization of Protection for Women And Child Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 30. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims. 33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

I. GENERAL

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high averaging per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases / acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious attention and handling.

In connection with this, the Government of Bengkayang Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Organization of Protection for Women And Child Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect. 11. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 15. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at: preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 17. Violence is any act that results in or causes suffering and distress whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 18. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss due to the actions of others. 23. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. I. GENERAL

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high averaging per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases / acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious attention and handling.

In connection with this, the Government of Bengkayang Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Organization of Protection for Women And Child Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

CHAPTER VIII

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 22

1. The Regent shall carry out control, guidance, and supervision of the organization of protection for victims of violence against women and children.
2. Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 12

1. Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 11 letter a include:
a. forming a network for prevention and handling of violence through coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
b. forming a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence;
c. organizing communication, information, and education about violence against women and children; and
d. socialization of laws and regulations related to violence against women and children.
2. Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner coordinated by the SKPD having duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment.

CHAPTER VII

REPORTING

Article 21

1. P2TP2A shall report prevention, handling and protection activities for women and child victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment.
2. The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment shall report prevention, handling and protection activities for women and child victims of violence to the Regent.
3. The Regent shall report protection of women and child victims of violence to the Governor.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

3.6.text: Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A for the Protection of Women and Children is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 26. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 27. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved. 28. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children. 29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims. 33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bengkayang Regency. 2. Regional Government is Bengkayang Regency as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkayang Regency. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Institution of Bengkayang Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 6. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government and regional government. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 8. Child with Special Needs is a child with special characteristics that differ from children in general without always indicating mental, emotional or physical disability, which includes among others: visually impaired, hearing impaired, mentally disabled, physically disabled, socially maladjusted, learning difficulties, behavioral disorders, gifted children, children with health disorders and disabled children. 9. Child Protection is all forms of activities to guarantee and protect children so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with dignity and humanity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect. 11. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 15. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at: preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 17. Violence is any act that results in or causes suffering and distress whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 18. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 19. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 20. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 21. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss due to the actions of others. 23. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 25.

Article 9

1. P2TP2A as referred to in Article 8 shall be established by the Regional Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of the Regional Government, non-governmental organizations, health service institutions, law enforcement officials, professional personnel, volunteer assistants, social workers, religious leaders, shelters, and social rehabilitation centers.
3. The membership of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

Article 19

1. In organizing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government shall include consultation, coordination, and reporting.
3. Cooperation with other regional governments and other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, and development of integrated service systems.

Article 2 letter a

What is meant by "respect for victims' rights" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights.

letter b

What is meant by "justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying development results.

letter c
What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.

letter d
What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration.

letter e

What is meant by "non-discrimination" means not making distinctions on any grounds or in any manner, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.

I. GENERAL

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high averaging per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases / acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious attention and handling.

In connection with this, the Government of Bengkayang Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Organization of Protection for Women And Child Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bengkayang Regency. 2. Regional Government is Bengkayang Regency as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkayang Regency. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Institution of Bengkayang Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 6. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government and regional government. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 8. Child with Special Needs is a child with special characteristics that differ from children in general without always indicating mental, emotional or physical disability, which includes among others: visually impaired, hearing impaired, mentally disabled, physically disabled, socially maladjusted, learning difficulties, behavioral disorders, gifted children, children with health disorders and disabled children. 9. Child Protection is all forms of activities to guarantee and protect children so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with dignity and humanity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect. 11. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 15. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at: preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 17. Violence is any act that results in or causes suffering and distress whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 18. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 19. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 20. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 21. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss due to the actions of others. 23. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 25.

Article 2 letter a

What is meant by "respect for victims' rights" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights.

letter b

What is meant by "justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying development results.

letter c
What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.

letter d
What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration.

letter e

What is meant by "non-discrimination" means not making distinctions on any grounds or in any manner, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.

Article 13

In addition to prevention efforts carried out by the Regional Government as referred to in Article 12, prevention efforts must also be carried out by:
a. family and closest relatives;
b. community and business sector; and
c. educational institutions.

1. In organizing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government shall include consultation, coordination, and reporting.
3. Cooperation with other regional governments and other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, and development of integrated service systems.

Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A for the Protection of Women and Children is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 26. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 27. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved. 28. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children. 29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims. 33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

I. GENERAL

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high averaging per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases / acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious attention and handling.

In connection with this, the Government of Bengkayang Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Organization of Protection for Women And Child Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

I. GENERAL

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high averaging per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases / acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious attention and handling.

In connection with this, the Government of Bengkayang Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Organization of Protection for Women And Child Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 6. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government and regional government. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 8. Child with Special Needs is a child with special characteristics that differ from children in general without always indicating mental, emotional or physical disability, which includes among others: visually impaired, hearing impaired, mentally disabled, physically disabled, socially maladjusted, learning difficulties, behavioral disorders, gifted children, children with health disorders and disabled children. 9. Child Protection is all forms of activities to guarantee and protect children so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with dignity and humanity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 14. Part Two

Cooperation

I. GENERAL

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high averaging per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases / acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious attention and handling.

In connection with this, the Government of Bengkayang Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Organization of Protection for Women And Child Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

Prevention Efforts

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 14. Violence is any act that results in or causes suffering and distress whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 18. I. GENERAL

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high averaging per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases / acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious attention and handling.

In connection with this, the Government of Bengkayang Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Organization of Protection for Women And Child Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

Article 18

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 11 letter f, shall include monitoring, documentation, and reporting of cases of violence against women and children.

Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss due to the actions of others. 23. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 25.

I. GENERAL

As we all know that protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs serious attention, particularly Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Bengkayang Regency.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high averaging per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this shows that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases / acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious attention and handling.

In connection with this, the Government of Bengkayang Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Organization of Protection for Women And Child Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.
